connections.why: Enzymes are proteins built from the molecules studied first
Glucose and other molecules are the substrates oxidised in respiration
Nucleic acid chemistry underpins DNA's role as the genetic code
Membrane structure governs how substances cross the cell surface
Cells must copy their contents before they divide
Specialised cells are organised into tissues and organs
Exchange and transport rely on diffusion, osmosis and active transport
Exchange surfaces and transport vessels are specialised organs
Exchange systems are adapted to an organism's size and habitat
Adaptation to niches generates the variety classification describes
Human activity reduces the biodiversity that sampling measures
Transport delivers the substances homeostasis must regulate
Nervous and hormonal coordination achieve homeostatic control
Both depend on cell signalling and molecular recognition
Biodiversity is measured within the ecosystems organisms occupy
Photosynthesis fixes the energy that flows through ecosystems
Enzymes catalyse the reactions of photosynthesis and respiration
Photosynthesis stores the energy respiration later releases
Understanding the genetic code makes gene technology possible
Meiosis generates the variation inheritance describes
Patterns of inheritance scale up to allele frequencies in populations
Selection over time produces the evolutionary trends seen in plants
Selection over time produces the evolutionary trends seen in animals
Skills built in the assessed tasks are tested in the AS practical paper
Skills built in the assessed tasks are tested in the A2 practical paper
